dedupe_keys.name: discharges to rivers from abandoned metal mines england environment agency

description: This Environment Agency dataset gives average flows and water quality for known mine water discharges from abandoned metal mines in England. It was adapted and updated from the 2012 report "Prioritisation of abandoned non-coal mine impacts on the environment: the national picture". For each discharge it records average flow (litres per second), pH, metal concentrations (mg/l) and metal flux (kg per year) for arsenic, cadmium, copper, iron, manganese, nickel, lead and zinc. It is one Excel file (2018 edition) downloaded free from the Environment Agency data service; the attribution statement reads "© Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2016. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): OGL-UK-3.0. Caveats: the provider says the data are known to be incomplete, and blank values mean either below detection or not measured. For simulation it quantifies the pollution load that abandoned mines put into rivers, useful for water quality, treatment prioritisation and flood remobilisation studies. Related catalogue records include the Mining Remediation Authority mine water treatment schemes and the Pollution Inventory (England).
